title: Conformance vector
description: One thing to check, and what it should produce. Vectors live in conformance/vectors/<subject>/<case>.json. A message subject uses the message name with each capital starting a new part, lower case and joined by hyphens, as its directory.

subject.description: What this vector checks. A transport vector checks that the packet header was built correctly, and whatever follows it is immaterial. A cipher vector checks the cipher alone and is not a packet.

message.description: Identity of the message these bytes carry. A message subject only.

version.description: Client version these bytes belong to, whichever end emitted them. Selects the revision.

bytes.description: The bytes on the wire, in hexadecimal, whitespace ignored. For a message this is the deciphered channel payload with its leading command byte. Bytes that identify a person are zeroed before committing.

fields.description: Every field the revision defines, under its own name. An integer narrower than 64 bits is a number; a 64 bit one is a decimal string, because JSON cannot hold it exactly. A 32 bit float is written as the value it reads back as, which is the double nearest to it and rarely the decimal somebody typed. A byte run is lower case hexadecimal. A string given a size drops the zero bytes padding it out, a terminated string drops its terminator and nothing else, and a remaining string drops nothing. A size counts bytes rather than characters. An array is an array, and a struct or a run of bits is an object keyed by its own names. A field a presence rule leaves out is written as null.

key.description: The key, in hexadecimal. A cipher subject only.

plaintext.description: Input to the cipher, in hexadecimal. A cipher subject only.

ciphertext.description: What the cipher produces, in hexadecimal. A cipher subject only.
